note: Existing-source, strict-license-screened public gallery. Additional historical photos remain held from this site. Anatomy overlays are teaching annotations, not a separate verified voucher determination.

tiles.heading: 01 · TUFT
tiles.details: Look at crown continuity and narrow inrolled blades. Foliage alone is not unique; capture entire clump connected to flowering stem. No photograph proves roots.
tiles.short: Dense perennial bunch, thin rolled leaves
tiles.status: TWO HABIT PHOTOS; NO ROOT EXPOSURE

tiles.heading: 02 · COLLAR
tiles.details: One attributed CC BY original now shows an opened blade/sheath junction with a visible pale papery flap consistent with a ligule. It has NO millimeter ruler; whether the exact free membrane measures 4–10 mm is NOT established by the photo. Compare a vouchered leaf collar with deergrass's generally shorter ligule before definitive ID.
tiles.status: ACTUAL OPENED LEAF-COLLAR PHOTO INSTALLED — MEMBRANE LENGTH AND TAXON STILL NEED VERIFICATION

tiles.heading: 03 · PANICLE
tiles.details: Two real source-attributed CC BY photos now show a narrow flowering head against fingers and densely gathered reproductive units close up. Literature reports panicle length 10–40 cm and width 0.6–2.4 cm. Branch insertions are not ruler-measured; deergrass may share a narrow head.
tiles.short: Narrow contracted head, not a rigid spike
tiles.status: MATURE FLOWERING-HEAD MACROS INSTALLED — RACHIS BRANCH LENGTH NOT MEASURED

tiles.heading: 04 · SPIKELET
tiles.details: One enlarged CC BY mature reproductive photo shows narrow units but DOES NOT certify which pieces are the 2–3 mm paired glumes versus the 3.8–5 mm lemma. Those lengths are published botanical traits, not pixel measurements. Need an independently determined ripe specimen under 10–20× with actual 1-mm scale.
tiles.short: One floret; glumes ~2–3 mm, lemma ~4–5 mm
tiles.status: REPRODUCTIVE CLOSE-UP INSTALLED — NO RULER-CALIBRATED DISSECTED SPIKELET

tiles.heading: 05 · DISSECT THE LEMMA, CALLUS AND AWN
tiles.details: The FNA treatment gives fertile lemmas about 3.8–5 mm, with an awn absent or to 6 mm; Kew GrassBase describes a 4–5 mm, three-veined lemma and a 0–4 mm awn. Preserve these source-specific ranges. Dissect a mature same-voucher spikelet: separate its two shorter one-veined glumes, expose the three-veined lemma, two-veined palea, hairy callus and any true awn attachment. An entire grass head, finger for scale, or undissected narrow floret is NOT proof of bract identity, awn origin or dimensions.
tiles.short: Fertile lemma about 3.8–5 mm; a single terminal awn may be absent or short.

tiles.heading: 06 · CENTRAL TEXAS LOOK-ALIKES + RELEASE GATE
tiles.details: Deergrass (M. rigens) has a generally shorter membranous ligule, often 0.5–2(3) mm in FNA, and typically a more rigid, spikelike panicle; pine muhly has a longer 4–10(12) mm ligule and usually less rigid flowering branches. Their lemma lengths overlap. Lindheimer muhly (M. lindheimeri) forms a much larger fountain-shaped bunch, and seep muhly (M. reverchonii) has a more open fine-textured panicle. Do not confuse accepted M. dubia with the held source name M. piniflora or certify county nativity from it. NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO: rooted local crown connected to mature head, 1-mm-calibrated true ligule, same-voucher 3.8–5 mm spikelet with both glumes, lemma, palea, callus and any awn, matched deergrass. NEEDS_SITE_QA: verify seven archived photos and comparison panels, research-grade/voucher vs provisional labels, all licenses/attribution, actual arrows and public mobile display. Retain FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS.
tiles.short: Separate deergrass by its shorter ligule and usually tighter panicle; don't rely on silhouette.

steps.title: 1 · First, recognize the plant
steps.look_for: Pine muhly (Muhlenbergia dubia): densely tufted narrow-leaved perennial with erect slender stems and a narrow contracted panicle. Confirm with membranous ligule (about 4–10 mm) and measured spikelets (about 3.8–5 mm); never identify from habit alone.
steps.why_it_matters: Start with the recorded recognition characters before making a species identification.

steps.title: 3 · Inspect leaves, collar and nodes
steps.look_for: One attributed CC BY original now shows an opened blade/sheath junction with a visible pale papery flap consistent with a ligule. It has NO millimeter ruler; whether the exact free membrane measures 4–10 mm is NOT established by the photo. Compare a vouchered leaf collar with deergrass's generally shorter ligule before definitive ID.
steps.why_it_matters: Examine the real structures; the photo may not expose or measure all the described characters.

steps.title: 4 · Check the flowering structure
steps.look_for: Two real source-attributed CC BY photos now show a narrow flowering head against fingers and densely gathered reproductive units close up. Literature reports panicle length 10–40 cm and width 0.6–2.4 cm. Branch insertions are not ruler-measured; deergrass may share a narrow head.
steps.why_it_matters: Use an attached, correctly identified specimen when deciding the flower or spikelet structures.

intro: Pine muhly (Muhlenbergia dubia): densely tufted narrow-leaved perennial with erect slender stems and a narrow contracted panicle. Confirm with membranous ligule (about 4–10 mm) and measured spikelets (about 3.8–5 mm); never identify from habit alone.
memory_rule: Narrow, erect contracted panicles and fine often rolled blades suggest pine muhly; confirm with true ligule and measured spikelets.
photo_data_caution: Missing or restricted comparison photographs have not been replaced by guesses. Source statements are not proof the associated structure is visible in any available photo.
